items.text: Brain activity predicting a "decision" occurs 300ms before subjects report awareness of choosing. This finding:

options.A: Has no bearing on free will—conscious experience is what matters
options.B: Suggests free will operates differently than we thought
options.C: Is concerning but doesn't definitively refute free will
options.D: Significantly undermines the case for free will
options.E: Demonstrates decisions are made by unconscious processes, not free choice

items.text: A man from an abusive home, with genetic aggression predispositions, raised in poverty, commits assault. His moral responsibility is:

options.A: Full—circumstances explain but don't excuse; he chose his actions
options.B: High—background is relevant but doesn't diminish responsibility much
options.C: Partial—circumstances constrained but didn't eliminate choice
options.D: Low—he's largely a product of forces beyond his control
options.E: Minimal—given his background, this outcome was nearly inevitable

items.text: The concept "could have done otherwise" is:

options.A: Clearly coherent—alternative choices were genuinely available
options.B: Meaningful as a practical concept even if metaphysically complex
options.C: Useful fiction that enables moral discourse
options.E: Definitely incoherent—all actions are determined by prior causes
